findings.title: A block-local binding hides a real outer call and yields a deletion proposal
findings.harm: A genuinely invoked function enters deadcode.safe and campaign delete steps. No deletion was executed.
findings.expected: The block-local target ends with its block; invoke calls the outer target.
findings.observed: No call/ref edge from invoke to target; no-known-incompleteness, zero diagnostics, target in safe and campaign delete.
findings.oracle: Controlled Node invocation returns1; Babel parses the block and outer call.
findings.before_P05: The earlier95bf source records invoke -> target correctly.
findings.repair_direction: Represent lexical block binding extents, not a whole-function shadow-name set. Verify inner and outer calls separately.

findings.title: JSX literal text becomes a phantom function and deletion proposal
findings.harm: A source edit proposal can remove UI text as if it were a function. No deletion was executed.
findings.expected: Only Page is a function declaration; function pretend() is JSXText.
findings.observed: pretend node extracted, no-known-incompleteness, zero diagnostics, safe tier and campaign delete step.
findings.oracle: Pinned Babel7.29.9 valid TSX AST: Page FunctionDeclaration and literal JSXText, no pretend declaration.
findings.before_P05: Same phantom definition exists in95bf. Edge masking fixed JSX child-text calls, not definition discovery.
findings.repair_direction: Use consistent executable-source masking for declaration discovery, usage scans and completeness diagnostics.

findings.title: A same-named parameter is mistaken for a global function
findings.harm: Wrong callers and impact can direct inspection at the wrong implementation.
findings.expected: invoke(target) calls its parameter, not the module target declaration.
findings.observed: invoke -> module target call edge; zero diagnostics.
findings.oracle: Controlled invoke(()=>7) returns7; Babel records target as the parameter binding.
findings.repair_direction: Resolve binding shadowing before same-file/import/global candidate selection for call kinds.

findings.title: Namespace JSX access reaches a private non-exported function
findings.harm: The graph invents a callable member that the imported namespace does not expose.
findings.expected: UI.Hidden has no exported binding; a real Visible control may resolve.
findings.observed: Page -> Hidden call edge with no diagnostic.
findings.oracle: Controlled ES-module namespace contains only Visible; Babel validates the JSX syntax.
findings.before_P05: 95bf did not produce this JSX edge; the new JSX member path introduced the invalid resolution.
findings.repair_direction: Resolve namespace export surfaces separately from default object/class member surfaces.

findings.title: A known function-value alias loses its invoking consumer
findings.harm: Impact includes the assignment/module reference but omits invoke; it can understate what changes.
findings.expected: Track the known target through const alias = target and alias().
findings.observed: Assignment ref retained, invocation relationship absent, no diagnostic; imported case retains coarse import but impact still misses invoke.
findings.oracle: Controlled Node invocation returns1 in both fixtures.
findings.before_P05: The local alias invocation is omitted in 95bf too. The imported alias variant was checked on current main; no older-source comparison is claimed for that variant.
findings.repair_direction: Track simple immutable callable aliases with reassignment/shadow controls, or explicitly report unsupported resolution.

findings.title: Python decorator use is absent from mapped dependencies
findings.harm: Changing a literal decorator has zero mapped impact on the decorated function.
findings.expected: Record or qualify the known @decorate dependency.
findings.observed: decorate and action nodes, no edges, no-known-incompleteness and zero diagnostics.
findings.oracle: Python ast records action.decorator_list with Name(decorate).
findings.repair_direction: Model literal decorator references separately from unknown framework dispatch.

findings.title: Incomplete analysis has inconsistent visibility and usefulness across tools
findings.harm: Warnings may disappear from machine-readable results, while usable partial information is discarded elsewhere.
findings.expected: One typed limitation contract across informational/advisory/decision surfaces, with explicit per-tool action semantics.
findings.observed: CLI find/explain return normal JSON exit0 without in-band analysis; MCP returns isError and status/analysis/hint without normal result. Context CLI retains typed useful partial data but MCP replaces it. Risk lacks in-band incompleteness on both transports. Impact/deadcode/review/diff retain typed limits.
findings.oracle: Identical known incomplete graph fed to actual CLI and long-lived MCP server; clean freshness rerun recorded.
findings.repair_direction: Shared analysis envelope; preserve useful informational partial results while action gates remain inconclusive.

count_semantics: Seven distinct issue families; aliases and requested-engine repetitions are not independent bugs.
